topic: The architectural evolution of AI Transformers (2017-2024)

facts.claim: The Transformer architecture was introduced in 2017 by Vaswani et al. in the paper 'Attention is All You Need', which eliminated recurrence and relied entirely on self-attention mechanisms to compute representations.

citation.source: Vaswani et al., Google Brain and Google Research

facts.claim: BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) was introduced by Google in 2018, using only the encoder part of the Transformer architecture and introducing bidirectional pre-training for language understanding tasks.

citation.source: Devlin et al., Google AI Language

facts.claim: GPT-2, released by OpenAI in 2019, demonstrated that decoder-only Transformers could achieve strong performance on language generation tasks with 1.5 billion parameters.
GPT-3, released in 2020, scaled the decoder-only Transformer architecture to 175 billion parameters and demonstrated few-shot learning capabilities without fine-tuning.

Vision Transformer (ViT) was introduced by Google Research in 2020, demonstrating that pure Transformer architectures could be applied directly to image patches for computer vision tasks, achieving state-of-the-art results.
The Switch Transformer, introduced by Google in 2021, scaled to over 1.6 trillion parameters using sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture while maintaining computational efficiency.
ChatGPT was launched by OpenAI in November 2022, using Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) to fine-tune GPT-3.5 for conversational interactions.
GPT-4, released in March 2023, introduced multimodal capabilities allowing the model to accept both text and image inputs, representing a significant architectural evolution in Transformer models.
LLaMA (Large Language Model Meta AI) was released by Meta in February 2023, offering open-access Transformer models ranging from 7B to 65B parameters trained on publicly available datasets.
Mistral 7B, released in September 2023, introduced grouped-query attention (GQA) and sliding window attention mechanisms to improve inference efficiency while maintaining strong performance.
Claude 3, released by Anthropic in March 2024, introduced a family of multimodal models with enhanced reasoning capabilities and extended context windows up to 200K tokens.
Gemini 1.5, announced by Google in February 2024, achieved a breakthrough with a context window of up to 1 million tokens using an efficient mixture-of-experts architecture.
